properties.areaDesc: Pearl River, MS
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 6:02AM CST until November 2 at 6:00PM CST by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Mississippi...

West Hobolochitto Creek Near McNeil affecting Pearl River County.

For the West Hobolochitto Creek...including McNeil...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...West Hobolochitto Creek near McNeil.

* WHEN...From early this morning to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, North Beech Road and Palestine Road in
Picayune will be impassable. Several homes will be flooded in
vicinity of the stream. Flooding threatens structures along MS
Highway 43 near the bridge and fills culverts and ditches along
bridge approach.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 AM CST Sunday the stage was 17.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:45 AM CST Sunday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.5 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 04/10/2021.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates are needed.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 1 at 6:53AM EST until November 1 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Bay County in the panhandle of Florida...

* Until 900 AM CST.

* At 553 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Panama City, Lynn Haven, Springfield, Hiland Park, Vicksburg,
Southport, Dirego Park and Cedar Grove.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:45AM MST until November 1 at 4:45PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Central Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 445 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Streams continue to rise due to excess
runoff from earlier and continuing rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 443 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Big Water, Henrieville, Bryce Canyon National Park, Kodachrome
Basin State Park, Coyote Creek, Wahweap Creek, the Paria River
from the headwaters to the Utah/Arizona state line, Buckskin
Gulch, Wire Pass, and the Paria Canyon area.
- Backcountry roads may be impassable.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

FFWLCH

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Evangeline Parish in central Louisiana...

* Until 745 AM CST.

* At 343 AM CST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 10 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Chicot State Park, Bayou Chicot, Indian Lake and St. Landry.

deaths occur in vehicles.

west-northwest long period swell is expected to combine with
lower, shorter period northwest and south-southwest swells.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These

them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:

remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.25 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Show Low, Pinetop-Lakeside, Lake of the Woods, White Mountain
Lake Estates, Linden, Wagon Wheel, North Fork, Pinetop Country
Club, McNary, Cedar Creek, Carrizo, Rainbow Lake, Indian Pine,
Hon-Dah, Show Low Regional Airport, White Mountain Apache
Reservation, Show Low Lake, Red Top Mountain and Woodland
Reservoir.

between mile markers 298 and 357. State Route 73 between mile
markers 311 and 326...and between mile markers 353 and 357. State
Route 61 between mile markers 353 and 356. State Route 77 between
mile markers 343 and 352.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory,
until 7 PM EST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory,
until 7 PM EST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 11:14PM MST until November 2 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall over saturated
soils.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain and isolated thunderstorms are expected Saturday night
through the early morning hours of Monday. An additional 1 to 4
inches of rain will be possible, on already saturated ground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or
paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still
decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger
station.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 12:08AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST early this morning through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected today into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely and some rivers may
flood. If river flooding materializes, it will likely continue
into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 1 at 1:57AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding and dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Yavapai, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 31 at 10:51PM MST until November 1 at 10:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring. Dangerous flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1048 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Overflowing poor drainage areas will cause minor
flooding in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Big Bug Creek, Agua Fria River, Black Canyon, Turkey Creek,
Castle Creek, Humbug Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Black Canyon City, Dewey-Humboldt, Cordes Lakes, Mayer, Spring
Valley, Crown King, Agua Fria National Monument, Poland Junction,
Lake Pleasant, Cordes Junction, Castle Hot Springs, Arcosanti,
Horse Thief Basin, Bumble Bee, Rock Springs, Cleator, Humbug,
Coles Bay and Humbug Bay.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 263 and 283. Interstate 17
between mile markers 242 and 268.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Turney Gulch Group Campground, Hazlett Hollow Campground and
Black Canyon Campground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 10:26PM MST until November 2 at 8:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Tonto Creek and flood-prone locations is
occurring. Low-water crossings are inundated with water and may not
be passable. Tonto Creek is expected to continue to slowly rise
over the next 12-24 hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1026 PM MST, a streamflow gauge on Tonto Creek north of Tonto
Basin is above action stage, with a stage height of 4.38 feet at
915 PM MST. Flooding is ongoing along Tonto Creek in the warned
area. Please use the Tonto Creek Bridge for all travel across the
creek. Bar X Crossing, and any other low water crossings, will
likely become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tonto Basin.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 31 at 10:07PM PDT until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.areaDesc: Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 11:03PM MDT until November 1 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef
National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake
Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected
across much of southern, southeast and east central Utah tonight
through Sunday.

Moist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result
in efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,
streams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will
likely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will
likely become impassable from this excessive runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Inland Palm Beach County; Metro Palm Beach County; Inland Broward County; Metro Broward County; Inland Miami-Dade County; Metropolitan Miami Dade; Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County; Far South Miami-Dade County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 12:43AM EDT until November 2 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
An upper-level low will move atop Florida today through Monday. This
feature will add more moisture and support for showers and storms
than recent days. Strong low-level easterly flow will result in bands
of repeated rainfall for isolated to scattered locations. Showers and
storms are expected to be a bit more widespread with higher rain
rates than the past few days.

* WHAT...Bands of heavy rain may cause urban and street flooding.

* WHERE...All of Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered area of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Uncertainty is high regarding exactly where the highest rain
amounts will fall. However, scattered locations across the east
coast may pick up 3 to 5 inches of rain through Monday. Isolated
spots may see accumulations as high as 5 to 7 inches. These
amounts may fall over a window of a few hours. Expected impacts
could be greater than forecast if the heaviest rainfall occurs
near the coast during times of high tide.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
counties, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin, and Brevard.

* IMPACTS...Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Some

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 2:09PM ChST until November 2 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 10 feet in the surf zone and
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...West and north facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM ChST Monday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Typhoon In-fa will send pulses of an elevated,
long-period, northwest swell over the next day or two. Surf of
6 to 8 ft today will return to advisory levels tonight, peaking
at 8 to 10 feet Monday morning. As such, the High Surf Advisory
and High Rip Current Risk Statement were extended at least
through Monday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 9:18PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST Sunday through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the South Fork of the Rio Grande, including South Fork and
Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org

properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent east-northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the
St John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead
to additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Saturday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.7 feet
Monday evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

...This is a PARTICULARY DANGEROUS SITUATION...

For the San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

.Significant and historic flooding is possible along the San Juan
River at Pagosa Springs. Widespread rainfall is expected to begin
early Sunday morning and continue through Monday morning. Excessive
runoff will also increase flooding risks. The region should prepare
for a dangerous and impactful flood event.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...major flooding is
forecast. This is a particularly dangerous situation.

* WHAT...Major flooding caused by excessive rainfall is forecast
along the San Juan River. This is a Particularly Dangerous
Situation.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Portions of San Juan Street are beginning
to flood.  Waters have reached the foundation of the Colorado
Ranger Building.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 17.0 feet early Monday morning.
It will then fall below flood stage Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 10/05/1911.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

enforcement.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 745 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 352 PM MST, An upstream floodgate release is expected to cause
flooding in the warned area.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Marketplace.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 241 PM MST, gauge reports indicated heavy rain due to Releases
upstream from Bartlett Dam. Flooding is already occurring in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rio Verde and Fort McDowell.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 30 at 11:51AM MDT until November 3 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River Near Cedar Hill affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Animas River near Cedar Hill.

* WHEN...Rises on the river are expected to begin Sunday night and
last through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.5 feet, Minor overbank flooding of low spots along
the river from the New Mexico-Colorado border down to the riverwalk
in Farmington can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Friday the stage was 6.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.2 feet
this afternoon. It will then rise to 9.9 feet late Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Action stage is 9.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

If you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding or
the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon MDT.
